commits.message:
Release an unsigned reservation whose decision a journal repair dropped

After the documented repair, which moves watcher-journals.sqlite aside,
a funding reservation can name a fault decision that the new journals
do not hold. A signed one already goes to the finality-gated orphan
settle. An unsigned one was skipped by every sweep, so its coins stayed
leased to the watcher forever.

The startup sweep now releases it. It runs before dispatch, so no run
is left to sign the reservation, and a fresh detection plans a fresh
reservation. Only that sweep passes `startup`. The idle sweep around
the journal_busy requeue and the per-run release run beside live work,
so they still leave such a reservation alone. Nothing is run,
resubmitted or rebuilt from chain facts, and workflow rows stay for
retention.

journal-repair-reservation-release.test.ts moves the journals aside as
the README repair does, then runs the real startup path. The unsigned
case failed before this change. The README now describes the release
and the settle.

Refs #895

Preset wallet inputs only when they narrow the wallet

Under the watcher's restricted funding signer, getUtxos lists only the
reserved plain funding and getCollateral only the reserved collateral.
Lucid takes collateral only from among preset wallet inputs. So about
twenty fault-proof builders that preset whenever carriage or reference
inputs existed, or always, had a funding coin picked as collateral.
The reservation's ordinary/collateral separation check then refused
the signed transaction, and the objective was quarantined and rebuilt
identically forever.

src/funding/plain-funding-output.ts now holds the one rule:

- stepWalletFunding picks the fee input and the wallet inputs;
- plainWalletInputs gives the wallet inputs alone, for builders with
  no fee input;
- both preset only the plain coins outside the given exclusions, and
  only when that removes something from the wallet's view. Under the
  restricted wallet that is never the case, so the reserved collateral
  survives.

A wallet that holds coins but no selectable plain coin now fails
clearly, instead of passing an empty preset that Lucid treats as none.

Every builder now uses these helpers. That removes excludeUtxo,
walletInputsExcludingChunks, which had 19 callers,
walletInputsExcludingReferences, the outRefsEqual re-export, and
datum-free pre-filters that selectFeeInput already applies. The chunk
sites now really keep chunks out of collateral, as their comment
claimed. No builder reads the wallet more often than before.

A lint rule refuses presetWalletInputs in fault-proof sources outside
the funding module, the validation-trace dispute and the unattested-block
removal, which own deliberate presets. Restricted-wallet
regressions for double-spend and input-existence failed with the
separation error before this change.

Refs #893

Prove a CEK writeBits failure and a staged failure with oversized operands

An honest challenger could not prove two group-7 one-step cases, so the
defender of a wrong outcome won by forfeit:

- a writeBits failure on an input of at most 512 words. The chain
  builder had no route for a semantic failure carrying a writeBits
  witness;
- a staged failure whose operand exceeds the chunk size. The planner
  threw "a staged failure's staged operands are not driven".

Group 7 now routes a writeBits failure through semanticFailureRoots and
then stagedWriteBitsLoop once per hop, as the validators accept it.
writeBitsHops takes the failure witness and reuses the success planner,
choosing the encoder per hop. isStagedOperandWitness covers staged
failures, so staging, the evidence hash and reference reads go through
the existing staged-step path. Groups 5 and 7 share one loop-tail
helper. No existing transcript changes.

core-routes.test.ts derives every wired route from the SDK over the real
blueprint and asserts that each group's planned routes equal them, so
an unplannable route fails the suite. Two emulator tests drive both
cases to the settle and convict the defender; both failed before this
change on the forfeit path.

Refs #891

Say when moving the watcher journal aside is enough to upgrade

A watcher with no queued or active proof upgrades to this release by moving its decision journal aside, as the journal repair already does, and keeps its funding store and follower facts. Only a watcher with a proof in flight needs a fresh data directory.

Hold every readiness reason in one catalogue

Readiness reasons were listed by hand in five places: the public
presentation census, the logging allow-list, the doc check, and two
redaction helpers. The lists had drifted. forced_admission_divergence
and settlement_reconcile_stuck leaked their detail text on public
profiles, and the validation-trace-defense codes were invisible to the
doc check.

readiness-catalogue*.ts is now the one table: 199 codes, each read from
the producer's own exported constant, list or type union, with its kind
and bounded parameter formats.

- The public presentation reduces to publicReadinessLine. It shows a
  row's code alone once it reaches a free-text parameter.
- The public logging allow-list derives from the catalogue.
- The doc check reads catalogue codes, so every reason and detail
  needs operator text. The 14 validation-trace-defense codes and ten
  other details that lacked it are now documented in
  endpoints-and-logs.md.
- The /readyz route fixture parses every line it returns against the
  catalogue.
- Eight codes that nothing emits leave the census and the allow-list.

Lease inspection, which /readyz, the pipeline status and reconcile
evidence read, no longer writes. It shows an active lease past its
expiry as failed, and leaves marking the row to the writers. A route
test asserts that GET /readyz issues no write.

The frame-pressure stages are exported from midgard-core, so the
catalogue derives its stage values instead of repeating them.

Refs #897

Read the predecessor event ledger once per block, not once per event

Three complete-replay paths rebuilt the block's event ledger from the
predecessor for every event they inspected, so a block's cost grew with
events times predecessor size.

- Resolved-output proofs now come from the trie the replay has already
  built, instead of a fresh ledger per output.
- detectLedgerRelativeMissingInputs walks the ledger lazily once per
  phase (forced, then L2), and still reports findings in source order.
  The no-reference-input and non-existent-input wrongful-rejection
  checks share the same walk.
- collectReplayFindings runs its detectors one after another, so the
  family replays no longer build their ledgers concurrently.

A new fixture scenario covers a forced event after a failed normal one,
and predecessor-ledger-replay-cost.test.ts pins one walk per block by
counting trie leaves.

Measured on the replay-cost benchmark:
- the previous view at 4k events: 637 s -> 1.55 s
- the 10k-event scan: 11.5 s -> 4.2 s
- peak RSS at most 1.84 GB

Refs #894

Let a watcher replace a stale fault decision and finish a proven correction

A watcher whose journaled fault decision differs from a fresh
classification of the same observation now supersedes it: once no signed
attempt for the header is unresolved, it releases the unused funding,
forgets the old decision and journals the fresh admitted one. A lock with
no matching target is reported instead of failing the pass.

The transition-trace decision digest now binds the events' content and the
hub's policy ids only, so ordinary L1 activity cannot change a decision's
identity. The evidence and artifact schemas move to a new version with no
migration; this release needs a fresh watcher journal.

When the on-chain record already proves a block fraudulent, the watcher
drives the existing removal from that record, from a Locked or an Idle
lock, avoiding coins held by funding reservations. An observe-only watcher
stays quiet on that path.

Do not rehydrate an observed block's commit as an unresolved submission

After a restart, startup hydration set the unconfirmed submitted-block tx
hash and its since-time for any active journal, ObservedWaitingStability
included. The confirmation had already observed that commit on L1, and
nothing cleared the hash again when local finalization recovery finalized
the journal first or the block had merged. An idle node then reported a
false unresolved_block_submission on /readyz, at once because the since-time
was the journal's old updated-at, and merge returned
skipped_unresolved_commitment until the node's next own confirmed commit.

Hydration now leaves both empty for an observed journal; the
local-finalization flag still holds merge until local finalization. The
confirmation clears both whenever no journal is active: every submission's
journal is durable and active before its broadcast, and commit and
confirmation share the L1 lock, so a hash no active journal holds is
resolved. The clear for an observed match moves into the observed branch.

Refs #896

Advance emulator tests until the ledger tip makes a deadline-bound step due

Submit now judges a lower bound that must lie past a deadline at the
observed ledger tip, which admits it only once the tip is the submit margin
past the deadline. The defense and watchdog emulator tests advanced one slot
past the deadline, so the expiry answered not_due and the strike was
deferred. They now advance with awaitEmulatorTipPastDeadline, and the
funding test also checks that one slot past expiry is still not due.

Take availability-challenge bounds from the ledger tip, not the wall clock

The availability-challenge commands and the watcher's availability steps set
their lower bound from the wall clock minus 60 s and submit straight to the
provider, so the ledger refused them whenever its last block was more than
about a minute old. Both now take their bounds from the observed ledger tip,
inside the windows the availability and correction-lock validators check,
through one SDK rule (daAvailabilityValidityWindow). A node command waits for
the next block when the tip has not reached its bound; the watcher defers the
step to a later pass (reported as stepsDeferred). Both refuse when the window
is closed or leaves no valid range. Timeout and expired settle stay at or
after the response deadline.

The ledger-tip helpers move from midgard-node to midgard-core so the node
and the watcher share them.

Hand the retained-DA runtime a parsed watcher config and never parse it again

A parsed DA peer carries its peer id, which the config parser does not
accept as input, so a parsed config copied before being handed on (as the
stack replay does to swap its socket path) was refused with unknown_field
at da.peers[0]. The retained-DA runtime, its owner, the libp2p transport and
the fault-proof replayed ledger now take an admitted WatcherConfig and do
not re-parse it; raw JSON is parsed once where it enters.

Wait for the ledger tip before submitting a transaction not yet due

The ledger tip only moves when a block arrives, so a transaction whose lower
bound sits a few slots past the tip cannot be judged by a slot-count sleep.
Commands now wait on the observed tip, re-reading it until it reaches the
lower bound, within the existing inline wait and the validity window; the
runtime defers as before. Lower bounds are backdated from the observed tip
instead of the wall clock (commit end time, operator activation, exits,
takeover, reserve payout history retirement, recover-bond).

The "slot source stalled" verdict and the one-shot post-wait re-plan are
deleted. Submission refuses a transaction built before its own lower bound.
A retryable tip read failure is read again on the tip refresh interval; a
staleness refusal still ends the wait.

Look up a journey's reference scripts at the deployment's address

The published block actor registered and activated its operator against
reference scripts it looked for at the publisher wallet's address. On the
devnet that wallet is the one that published them, but a stack's fault
drill funds the journey from its own drill wallet while the stack's
reference wallet holds the scripts, so registration failed with "Missing
reference script". The actor and the deposit-trace successor now use the
manifest's referenceScriptDeployAddress, which is the same address on
the devnet.

Bring the acceptance docs in line with the rehearsal profile and cycle

The acceptance skill names the preprod-rehearsal profile beside
preprod-testing and preprod-public, and says a rehearsal run needs the
public section too. The example rehearsal config gives the reference
wallet minimum as 43,000 ADA, which is what a full rehearsal spends.
The Preprod stack guide describes the cycle as it now runs: transfer
completion at commit, then a settlement step that checks the deposit's
settlement and the transfer's merge and finality.

Count a node held only by its operator's activation as up

A node whose registered operator is not yet active answers /readyz with
503 and the reason "operator_not_yet_active". The attached stack's
services step read that endpoint through getJson, which drops every
non-2xx body, so it polled until its deadline and never reached the
operator step that activates the node. The runtime reconcile had the
same blind spot.

Both now read /readyz through getReadiness, which keeps a 503 body, so
nodeIsReady can accept a node that waits only for its activation. The
test fixtures answer as such a node, and two tests cover a run stopped
between registering and activating its operator.
